newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Verplaetse sees Britain joining EMU late.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Verplaetse sees Britain joining EMU late.

text.p: Belgian National Bank Governor Alfons Verplaetse said on Thursday that Britain would probably delay signing up to the European Union's planned single currency.
Economic and monetary union (EMU) is due to be launched on January 1, 1999, but the British government has yet to decide whether it will take part.
"I don't believe at all that the British will want to join (EMU) on January 1, 1999," Verplaetse told a Flanders Technology International Foundation lunch.
But he added he believed Britain would eventully join and that Europe needed Britain "but more politically."
"Sooner than we think the British, who can calculate well, who are super diplomats, will join EMU," he said.
"That's why I say 'wait for the right time but please let us get on, without you (the British)'," he said.
